messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Sundial (single-tenant) p99 latency breach detected for streaming endpoints — current p99: 4.8s (SLO: 2.0s). Trigger: tail-latency >= 2x baseline for 3m. Pager: Sam (oncall).

Sam (oncall): paging in. seeing a bunch of customer-reported stalled streams. first pass — is this a routing/regional issue or model hotpath? @Elin can you grab the traces?

Elin (sre): on it. loading traces now. quick look: multiple sessions show stall on chunk_write -> kernel queue wait. stack suggests token emission pauses around identical 8-12 token boundaries. p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~4.8s. concurrency for Sundial jumped from 20->480 over 12m.

Mohit (infra): thanks. checking node-level metrics. gpu-util on their dedicated pool is 98% on a subset of hosts. memory pressure moderate, but io_wait spikes on a few nodes. suspected KV cache thrash?

Sarah (eng-runtime): that pattern (8-12 token stalls) rings like long-prefix KV cache misses + re-warm under high concurrency. Could be burst of new prefixes for Sundial. Any prompt pattern from customer? @Alex?

Alex (cust-success): Sundial says they rolled a batch of new prompts for a QA experiment ~10:20 UTC, many long instruction prefixes (~1.2k tokens). They also enabled aggressive sampling in client which opens parallel sessions.

Sam (oncall): OK likely single-tenant prompt storm + high concurrency causing KV cache thrash + kernel queue backpressure. Immediate mitigations anyone?

Elin (sre): propose soft mitigations in this order: 1) apply per-tenant concurrency cap to Sundial routing (limit to 60) 2) enable model-fallback to a lower-memory variant for new sessions 3) increase batching window temporarily to 40ms to improve throughput.

Sarah (eng-runtime): agree. also push a short-lived policy to force prefix caching eviction for prefixes older than 2h to free slot churn. but that touches KV state; prefer to avoid unless needed.

Mohit (infra): I can attach autoscale burst for the dedicated pool (+3 nodes) but that takes ~90s to boot and warm. Should do it in parallel if we cap concurrency.

Sam (oncall): do the concurrency cap first. Mohit kick off burst. Sarah configure fallback. Elin monitor. Alex coordinate with Sundial to reduce client parallel sessions if they can.

Alex (cust-success): messaging Sundial now: asking to pause the QA rollout and throttle to <50 concurrent sessions. ETA from them ~3m.

incident-bot: action recorded: concurrency-cap applied to routes/sundial/* -> max_concurrency=60 by Sam.

Sarah (eng-runtime): applying model fallback rule: route new sessions from customer:sundial to model:x64-medium-quant (compatible) for 15m. will send config:```
PATCH /routing/policies/sundial
{ "fallback_model": "x64-medium-quant", "duration": 900 }
```

Sarah (eng-runtime): applied. also extended batching window to 40ms for that pool.

Mohit (infra): started scale-up for pool sundial-dedicated. provisioning 3 gpus (p4d-like). logs show nodes booting.

Elin (sre): looking at traces after caps/fallback — p95 dropped to 0.9s within 120s, p99 to 1.6s. streaming stalls still visible on ~2 hosts. digging into logs for those containers.

Jules (ml-eng): can we get a sample prompt blob? suspect long prefix + uncommon tokens causing long tokenization path or weird kernel path.

Alex (cust-success): pasted sample prompt to #secure (sent to eng only). sample shows long system and context tokens + many special delimiters.

Sarah (eng-runtime): replicated locally with similar model variant after forcing concurrency load — reproduced the pause at token boundary 10-12. Kernel profiler shows repeated small kernel launch overhead because KV cache misses cause multi-stage attention recompute. Looks like cache region eviction thrash.

Elin (sre): workaround: increase per-worker KV cache capacity parameter for pool nodes to reduce churn. That requires a rolling config but can be applied to the pool quickly. Risk: higher memory usage; these nodes have wiggle room. Recommend +20% caching for 10m window.

Mohit (infra): patching nodes now: set env REDWOOD_KVCACHE_RATIO=1.2 on sundial pool agents and rolling restart of a subset (2 at a time). will coordinate.

Sam (oncall): be cautious with restarts during high load — do 1 at a time and drain connections. Use `route:shrink` to avoid client-side retries.

Mohit (infra): agreed. commands I'm running:```
for node in $(get-pool-nodes sundial-dedicated); do
  kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --force
  kubectl set env daemonset/sundial-agent REDWOOD_KVCACHE_RATIO=1.2
  kubectl uncordon $node
  sleep 45
done
```

Elin (sre): after the first node patch p99 immediate drop to 1.3s, second node drop to 1.1s. after 4 nodes patched p99 ~1.0s and stalls mostly gone.

Alex (cust-success): Sundial confirms they paused their rollout and throttled concurrency. They reported degraded UX but it's acceptable to stop the experiment. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: note: autoscale burst completed — 3 nodes added to sundial-dedicated pool.

Sarah (eng-runtime): follow-up: schedule a controlled KV cache sizing increase for dedicated pools with known single-tenant heavy prefixes. We'll add a config knob to autosuggest based on prefix churn. Jules, can your team add detection?

Jules (ml-eng): yes — we can add a metric for prefix-new-ratio and a heuristic to recommend cache ratio. I'll PR an eval to the monitor repo.

Sam (oncall): current status: p95=0.8s, p99=1.0s, error rate normal, streaming stalls largely mitigated. Sundial still at reduced concurrency; recommend keep policy until morning and follow-up with customer.

Alex (cust-success): Sundial requests an incident summary and ask for guidance for future rollouts. I'll coordinate a postmortem call tomorrow.

Elin (sre): postmortem checklist: - root cause: prompt storm + high concurrency causing KV cache thrash + kernel queue backpressure - remediation: concurrency cap, fallback model, temporary cache ratio bump, autoscale burst - long-term actions: prefix churn metric + autosuggest, heatmap of prefix sizes per customer, safer defaults for single-tenant pools.

Sam (oncall): I'll close the paging but leave thread open for postmortem. Good job team. :teamheart: 

incident-bot: incident resolved (partial mitigations applied). Severity: Sev2. Duration: 22m.
